ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To present in full is to bring the whole matter forward without leaving a remainder; the phrase appears in questions, answers, and appraisals of complete presentation.
EvidenceBody: Literally, to raise or present in full. Yunmen Wenyan supplies the decisive contrast: seeing no single form is only half-presentation, and even then one must know the occasion of full presentation . Shengyin Chongkai pairs presentation across past and present with the ancestral master's true command . Juelang Dasheng joins the flower at Vulture Peak and snow at Shaoshi with separate transmission personally shown and the true command fully presented . Yuanwu Keqin raises the command in full and publicly asks how it can be unfolded. Liao'an Qingyu says that the entrustment at Vulture Peak is precisely here and tells the assembly to take up one fully presented saying ; Shending Yunwai Ze similarly says that if one can present it whole with bare hands, ease is assured . Zen bends the ordinary sense of completeness toward teaching-seat language: a saying, command, or lineage entrustment is brought forward without remainder and submitted to the assembly.
